description:
Potato chips are a common human snack, but they are not a good treat for cats. While a plain potato chip won't immediately poison your cat, chips are loaded with salt and fat that a cat's body simply isn't built to handle.

The biggest issue is the high salt content. If a cat eats too many chips, the extra sodium can draw water out of their body's cells, leading to severe dehydration and extreme thirst. In large amounts, this can cause salt toxicity, which may lead to vomiting, diarrhea, tremors, or kidney damage.

Additionally, many flavored chips contain onion or garlic powder, both of which are highly toxic to cats and can damage their red blood cells. Because of the heavy salt, unhealthy fats, and risk of hidden toxins, it is best to keep all potato chips away from your cat. Contact a veterinarian if your cat eats chips flavored with onion or garlic.

name: Potato chips
safetyNotes: Sodium hazard: potato chips contain 100–200mg of sodium per serving — far exceeding the safe daily sodium intake for cats
Hidden toxins: onion-flavoured, BBQ, and sour cream chips often contain onion or garlic powder — both toxic to cats
Fat and calorie hazard: regular feeding contributes to obesity and digestive upset
A single chip licked by a cat is unlikely to cause harm; a significant amount or flavoured chips warrants attention
Contact your vet if your cat eats onion- or garlic-flavoured chips in any quantity

symptoms.name: Salt Toxicity (Hypernatremia)
symptoms.notes: Because potato chips are heavily salted, they expose cats to dangerous levels of sodium. An overdose of sodium draws fluid out of the body's cells, leading to severe systemic dehydration and electrolyte derangements. In the brain, this rapid water loss causes cells to shrink and pull away from the skull.
symptoms.onset: Within minutes to several hours of ingestion

symptoms.name: Gastrointestinal Upset
symptoms.notes: The heavy salt and oil load of potato chips can irritate a cat's digestive system, causing vomiting and diarrhea.
symptoms.onset: Within a few hours of ingestion

symptoms.name: Hemolytic Anemia (From onion/garlic-flavored chips)
symptoms.notes: Onion and garlic powder in flavored chips cause oxidative damage to feline red blood cells (Heinz-body/hemolytic anemia); powdered forms are more concentrated and more dangerous.

symptoms.name: Solanine Toxicosis (If chips were made from green/unpeeled potatoes)
symptoms.notes: The raw potato contains the glycoalkaloid solanine to deter predators. While cooking and peeling potatoes to make chips removes the vast majority of this toxin, chips inadvertently made from green tubers or unpeeled potatoes may still contain residual glycoalkaloids. These trace toxins can disrupt cell membranes.

treatments.description: The veterinarian will measure the cat's serum sodium concentration and administer specific IV fluids to slowly restore the animal's normal water and electrolyte balance over a period of 2 to 3 days.
treatments.name: Controlled Sodium Correction (For severe Salt Toxicity)
treatments.notes: It is critical that the veterinarian lowers the serum sodium concentration slowly (at a recommended rate of 0.5 to 1.0 mEq/L per hour). If fluids are given too rapidly and the sodium drops too fast, it reverses the osmotic gradient, drawing water into the brain cells.

treatments.description: of the procedure: If the cat is exhibiting severe neurological distress, the veterinarian will administer anti-seizure medications (such as diazepam) to control convulsions. treatments.name: Neurological Emergency Management (If Salt Toxicity causes brain swelling)
treatments.notes: This is an urgent, life-saving intervention required if the rapid fluid shift from sodium ion poisoning has already caused the brain cells to shrink and trigger intracranial micro-hemorrhages or seizures.

treatments.description: of the procedure: If the ingestion is caught very early (within 1 to 2 hours) and the cat is asymptomatic, the veterinarian may induce vomiting to empty the stomach56. For acute salt ingestion before clinical signs appear, the vet may also ensure the cat has access to fresh water in small, frequent amounts to begin safe, natural hydration6. treatments.name: Early Gastrointestinal Decontamination (If caught immediately)
treatments.notes: Pet owners must never attempt to induce vomiting at home. Furthermore, activated charcoal does not effectively bind to salt, so its use would primarily be a precaution against other potential toxins (like trace solanine or onion/garlic powder flavorings).

treatments.description: If the chips were made from green or unpeeled potatoes and the cat shows signs of solanine toxicosis (such as a slow heart rate or severe hypersalivation), the veterinarian may administer atropine to partially compensate for the toxin's effect on the nervous system.
treatments.name: Cholinergic Symptom Management (If trace solanine is present)
treatments.notes: Because the cooking process breaks down the vast majority of solanine, this specific treatment is rarely needed for commercial potato chips unless they were severely undercooked or made from highly sprouted potatoes.
